items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: And then Muddy Waters kind of took that to Chicago and then that was another thing with electric guitars and everything.

ctx.x: Yeah. Like you have to get over that.

Exactly. But it’s just so heartfelt and the nuance was so amazing. And they were living that and — I introduced some of my young trumpet players at Eastman to some of this stuff and I had this kid come up to me and he said, “I don’t like this stuff but I sure am glad you’re playing it for me.” And I thought man, I was the same way. But I mean it’s not the beginning of the blues certainly. Because that was in the 30s when those guys were — you know. And then Muddy Waters kind of took that to Chicago and then that…
I forget how many times I’ve read this quote that goes something like, “jazz is America’s only true art form.” And I always say, “what about the blues?”
